column1: # The gate's page coverage record (#1382). One row per page view; hand-edited, and
# NOT generated by tool/overflow_baseline.sh — nothing here is a sweep output.
# rule a file named *_view.dart directly inside a views/ directory, at any depth under lib/page/
# ms_per_cell measured milliseconds per cell of this page's 9 widths x 26 locales; `-` means NOT MEASURED
# fixture_debt a `-` on a queued row is #1370's finding that no fixture gets that view past its loader yet
# basis section 11.2's: an isolated --plain-name run, its coordinate tests only, over one page's cells
# basis-note Every figure below was taken while a page was 8 widths x 26 locales = 208 cells. #1372 made
# basis-note it 9 x 26 = 234 on 2026-08-26 and did NOT re-measure this column: a per-cell rate is the
# basis-note quantity that survives a width being added, and the widest cells are the cheapest to lay
# basis-note out. Re-measure before planning a wave against a total rather than a rate.
# basis-note #1377 took the same quantity from --reporter json's per-test durations instead of
# basis-note wall-clock-minus-control: the control is a ~6s startup with ~1s of variance, and
# basis-note subtracting it from a ~9s total has a wider error band than the drift being measured.
# basis-note Cross-checked on the five pages it re-measured; four agreed with #1370 within 6%.
# basis-note So the 13 queued figures still carry #1370's wall-clock-minus-control reading and
# basis-note the 16 swept ones carry the durations; the agreement above is why one column holds both.
# basis-note #1378 kept that basis and added a rule: three runs, median committed. Four passes over
# basis-note pnp_entry read 21.2, 18.5, 11.6 and 10.9 ms/cell, because the first coordinate test of a
# basis-note run absorbs the font load and the first pump, and that fixed cost is most of a cheap
# basis-note page's total. Only 1 of its 7 comparable pages landed inside #1377's +/-7% floor
# basis-note (pnp_modem_lights_off, -2.3%); the rest moved -70% to +63%. Two causes, not one: below
# basis-note ~20ms/cell the two bases disagree by more than they agree, and pnp_static_ip's +63%
# basis-note (36.5 -> 59.6) is a fixture difference — this wave's state expands the DNS rows, so five
# basis-note IPv4 fields render where #1370's default state rendered three. So read any figure under
# basis-note ~20ms/cell as +/-40%, and re-measure before planning against one.
# unblocked pnp_setup_view was the one row this register has carried as measured-but-queued, and it is
# unblocked kept here because the distinction is the useful part: it was never fixture debt.
# unblocked pnpWizardConfiguringState in test/mocks/test_data/scenes/pnp_scene_data.dart got it past its
# unblocked loader on the first attempt and #1378 measured all 208 cells through it — 208 of 208 red at
# unblocked +12.0px on this page's 3-step wizard, on ui_kit v2.40.1's AppStepper bar variant, which
# unblocked divided constraints.maxWidth while AppFocusIndicator padded each bar by ringOffset=2.0
# unblocked unconditionally. Section 8's graduation rule is what kept it out: a whole page of debt does
# unblocked not enter the gate, and the only fixture that laid out clean was a 1-step wizard, i.e. one
# unblocked rendering no AppStepper. Filed as linksys/privacyGUI-UI-kit#70, fixed there by 936c1da6 and
# unblocked released as v2.40.2 on 2026-08-26; the tripwire in
# unblocked test/page/instant_setup/views/pnp_setup_view_test.dart went red with an empty incident list
# unblocked on the bump, which is the signal it was written to give, and was then deleted. Swept the
# unblocked same day, so this row's disposition is the shorter half of its story.
# rows sorted by path, so adding a page is a one-line diff
# doc doc/testing/overflow_gate_architecture.md section 11.5; the onboarding queue is section 11.6
